source.description: Long-form Japanese video benchmark supplied for local development. High-confidence rows are primary; generated/interpolated timing remains explicitly qualified by the reference pack.

annotations.reviewNote: Apoze accepted the supplied bilingual reference as authoritative for the decision corpus on 2026-08-02. Source confidence and interpolation qualifiers remain unchanged.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: なんか2人、かっこいいのついとるわ、背中に。
turns.english: You two have something cool-looking on your backs.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: あー、ついてない感じか。
turns.english: Oh, so it looks like I don't have it?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: わかんない、それ。
turns.english: I don't know what that is.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: あちゃー。
turns.english: Oof.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: この、なんか……どこ指してるの？ どこ指してるの？
turns.english: Like... where are you pointing? Where are you pointing?
turns.note: ASR and context; not fully shown in the edited captions

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: レイドさんのミラージュのポーズも相まって、ちょっと……。
turns.english: And with Reid's Mirage pose on top of that, it's kind of...

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: たしかに「あちゃー」って言ってる。「あちゃー」ってポーズしてる、こっちの画面では。
turns.english: It really does look like he's saying, “Oh no.” On my screen, he's doing an “oh no” pose.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: たぶんレイドさんの画面は胸張ってるけどな。
turns.english: I bet on Reid's screen he's puffing his chest out, though.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: マジで口に手当てて「あちゃー」ってしてるよね。
turns.english: He's seriously got a hand to his mouth like, “Oh no,” right?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 知ってる。
turns.english: I know.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: レジェンドに行けばいいのか、これ。そう、レジェンドで。
turns.english: Do I go to Legends for this? Yeah, under Legends.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 本当だ、なにこれ。
turns.english: You're right—what is this?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: オーラ、これ。
turns.english: This aura?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: おお、シルバー。
turns.english: Oh, Silver.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: シルバーなんだが。
turns.english: It says Silver, though.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 大丈夫？ 俺、なんか知らないけど、ずっと反映されなくて、ルーキーだったから。
turns.english: Is that okay? Mine wasn't updating for some reason, so it kept showing Rookie.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: え、待って、ゆいぴもルーキーじゃん。
turns.english: Wait, Yui-pi is Rookie too.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 俺、ルーキーやん。
turns.english: I'm Rookie too.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: え、これルーキーなの？
turns.english: Wait, this is Rookie?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: ルーキーだろ。
turns.english: That's Rookie.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: え、これ白いのにシルバーじゃないの？
turns.english: Wait, it's white—doesn't that mean Silver?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: いやいや、もう三角一個しかついてないやん。
turns.english: No, no—you've only got one triangle.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: バグってるよ。
turns.english: It's bugged.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: しょぼすぎ。
turns.english: That's so pathetic.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: しかも、ゆいぴさ、左上のレベル2じゃない？
turns.english: And Yui-pi, doesn't it say Level 2 in the top left?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: なにが？ どこ？
turns.english: What? Where?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: え、本当だ。レベル2やん。
turns.english: Oh, you're right. It says Level 2.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: え？
turns.english: Huh?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: バグり散らかしてない？
turns.english: Isn't it completely bugged out?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: いや、だから何もわからない。
turns.english: See? I don't understand any of this.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: サブアカやめてください。
turns.english: Please stop using a smurf account.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 本アカでやるとランク下がりそうだから、サブアカ持ってきたタイプでしょ、これ。
turns.english: This looks like the kind of thing where you brought a smurf because you were afraid your main account's rank would drop.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: やば。
turns.english: That's bad.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 終わってる。無敵の人じゃん、うち。いや、マジで。
turns.english: I'm finished. I'm acting like I've got nothing left to lose. Seriously.
turns.note: caption-verified; 無敵の人 is slang for someone with nothing to lose

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 今日、タイトルに「何もわからない」って書いてて、サムネにも「何もわからない」っていう保険張りながら来てます。
turns.english: Today I put “I don't understand anything” in the title, and even wrote it on the thumbnail as a disclaimer before coming here.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: たそまるにめっちゃ聞いたの。「うち、本当にエペできないけどいいの？」って。誘ってもらったけど、「大丈夫？ うち本当にわかんないよ」ってめっちゃ聞いて。「大丈夫！」って言われて来てるから。
turns.english: I asked Tasomaru over and over: “I seriously can't play Apex—is that okay?” She invited me, but I kept asking, “Are you sure? I genuinely don't know what I'm doing.” She said, “It's fine!” so that's why I'm here.
turns.note: caption-verified; エペ is shorthand for Apex Legends

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: だって、このメンバーだよ。
turns.english: Look who the group is.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: まあ、大丈夫でしょ。
turns.english: We'll be fine.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 全然関係ないんですけど。
turns.english: This is completely unrelated, but...

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: うん。
turns.english: Mm-hm.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: ずっと、何年間くらいだろう。6、7年間くらいiPhone XR使ってて。
turns.english: For—how many years was it?—I used an iPhone XR for about six or seven years.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: おお。XRか。
turns.english: Oh, an XR.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 画面もカメラもバキバキのまま頑張って使ってたんですけど、ついに17 Pro Maxになりまして。
turns.english: I kept using it even though the screen and camera were both completely cracked, but I've finally upgraded to a 17 Pro Max.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: うわー、一番いいやつやん。
turns.english: Whoa, that's the top-of-the-line one.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: Pro Maxって、でかいやつ？
turns.english: Is the Pro Max the big one?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: そう。なんかよくわかんないから、一番名前すごそうなやつにした。
turns.english: Yeah. I didn't really understand the options, so I picked the one with the most impressive-sounding name.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 待って、でかいやつなんだ、しかも。
turns.english: Wait—so you got the huge one too?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: Pro Maxだから、でかいんじゃない？
turns.english: It's a Pro Max, so isn't it the big one?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 17、17 Pro、17 Pro Maxがあって。
turns.english: There are the 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: うん。
turns.english: Yeah.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: なんかよくわかんないから、強そうなやつに。強そうなやつに。
turns.english: I didn't know, so I went with the one that sounded powerful. The powerful one.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 「この店で一番いいやつください」でPro Max？
turns.english: So you basically said, “Give me the best one in the store,” and got a Pro Max?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: そう、Pro Maxにして。なんか容量もわかんないから、1TBみたいな。一番でかいやつにしてくださいって。
turns.english: Yeah, I chose the Pro Max. I didn't understand the storage options either, so I got, like, 1 TB. I just said, “Give me the biggest one.”

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: やばい、もう富豪の買い方やん。
turns.english: That's wild—that's how a tycoon shops.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: なんかわかんなくて。
turns.english: I just didn't understand it.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: でも、私も去年買い替えたんだけど、それまでずっと11 Pro使ってたわ。
turns.english: I upgraded last year too, but before that I'd been using an 11 Pro the whole time.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 今は15かな。
turns.english: I think mine's a 15 now.
turns.note: caption-verified; overlapping edited captions made the raw speaker detector ambiguous

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 俺も去年、Xから16に変えたよ。
turns.english: I upgraded from an iPhone X to a 16 last year too.
turns.note: caption-verified; X is the model name, not “ten” here

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: おお。え、じゃあ結構近かったんだ（笑）。
turns.english: Oh! So we were pretty close, then. [laughs]

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: みんな近い。みんな結構近い。うん。
turns.english: We were all pretty close. Really close.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: いや、別にね、Xでね、いけてたんだよな。使えるんだよね。
turns.english: Honestly, the X was still fine. You can keep using it.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: いけてた。俺、画面も割れてなかったし。
turns.english: It was fine. My screen wasn't even cracked.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 私も割れてない。
turns.english: Mine wasn't cracked either.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: もうさ、まだ1週間くらいなんだけど、もうちょっとフィルターにヒビ入っちゃって。
turns.english: I've only had this one for about a week, and I've already put a crack in the screen protector.
turns.note: caption-verified; フィルター means the screen protector

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: なんで？ なんで？
turns.english: How? Why?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 使い手に問題があるよな、こういうの。
turns.english: In cases like this, the user is clearly the problem.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 落とした？
turns.english: Did you drop it?

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 落としちゃった（笑）。
turns.english: I did. [laughs]

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 私もよく落とすけど、画面までは割れないな。
turns.english: I drop mine a lot too, but the actual screen doesn't crack.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: マジ？
turns.english: Seriously?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: フィルターは割れるけど。
turns.english: The protector cracks, though.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: そうそう。フィルターが割れた。画面はまだいってないはず。
turns.english: Right, right. It's the protector that cracked. The screen itself should still be okay.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: こういう人のためにあるんだな、フィルターとかって。
turns.english: So screen protectors really are made for people like you.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: フィルターないと怖いね、使うの。
turns.english: I'd be scared to use a phone without one.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: え、そう？ 俺、フィルターつけてないし、なんならカバーもつけてない。
turns.english: Really? I don't use a screen protector—or even a case.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: ええ!?
turns.english: What?!

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 怖っ！
turns.english: That's terrifying!

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: それ、つるって落としたら、バリっていきますよ。
turns.english: If it slips out of your hand, it'll shatter.
turns.note: caption-verified; つるっ and バリッ are mimetic sound words

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 落とさないもん、そもそも。
turns.english: I don't drop it in the first place.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 私、ガチで落とす。
turns.english: I seriously drop mine all the time.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: わかる。手、滑るよね。
turns.english: I get it. Your hand just slips.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: もう、握力が……。
turns.english: My grip strength is already...

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: コップも、お茶もめっちゃこぼすんよな。
turns.english: I spill cups and tea all the time too.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: エマばあ。マジでばあさん。エマばあ。
turns.english: Grandma Ema. You're seriously an old lady. Grandma Ema.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: マジでばあさんなんだよ。
turns.english: I really am an old lady.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: コップは落とさないかも。
turns.english: I might not actually drop cups.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: もう何回、配信部屋でお茶ぶちまけたか。
turns.english: But I've lost count of how many times I've spilled tea all over my streaming room.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 最近、口元ゆるいんだよな。
turns.english: My mouth's been getting loose lately.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: わかる。口元も緩い。
turns.english: I know. Mine is too.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: ゆいばあ！
turns.english: Grandma Yui!

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 口からお茶、飛び出る。
turns.english: Tea just comes flying out of my mouth.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: わかる。なんか水こぼれる。
turns.english: I know. Water just spills out somehow.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: やだよ。
turns.english: I hate that.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: もう退化してんだよね。
turns.english: We're already regressing.
turns.note: caption-verified; corrected from ASR 耐火

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: そうなんだよね。
turns.english: Exactly.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 人間、最終的に赤ちゃんに戻っていくって言うからね。
turns.english: They say humans eventually go back to being babies.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: もう切り返したのか。
turns.english: You've already started turning back?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: そう、早いやろ。
turns.english: Yeah. Pretty early, right?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 早すぎやろ。
turns.english: Way too early.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: やっぱね、使わないとっていうか、動かないと退化していくんだなって。
turns.english: I guess if you don't use things—if you don't keep moving—they really do deteriorate.
turns.note: caption-verified; corrected from ASR 耐火

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: いや、でも別に、口元だけは一番動かしてるだろ、むしろ。
turns.english: But your mouth is probably the part you move the most.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 確かに。
turns.english: True.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: その辺の人間より。
turns.english: More than the average person, even.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 確かに。
turns.english: True.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: そこで劣化し始めたら、もう終わりよ。
turns.english: If that starts deteriorating, it's all over.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 確かに。
turns.english: True.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 気抜いたら鼻水出てくる。
turns.english: The second I let my guard down, my nose starts running.
turns.note: caption-verified; corrected from ASR 気づいたら

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: え？ 鼻水？
turns.english: Huh? A runny nose?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 気抜いたら鼻水出るから、ティッシュ詰めるわ。
turns.english: My nose runs whenever I relax, so I'm stuffing tissue in it.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: うわ、よくないよ。逆流するよ。
turns.english: That's not good. It'll flow back.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 逆流したらよくないの？
turns.english: Is it bad if it flows back?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 逆流して、喉がただれる。
turns.english: It'll run back and irritate your throat.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: ああ、そういうこと？
turns.english: Oh, that's what you mean?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: でも、小さい頃めっちゃズルズル吸ってたな。
turns.english: I used to sniff it back constantly when I was little.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: わかる。「やめなさい、あんた」って。
turns.english: I know. They'd say, “Stop that, you.”

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 言われる？ 「かみなさい」って。
turns.english: Did they tell you that too? “Blow your nose.”
turns.note: ASR corrected; かむ means blowing one's nose here

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: でもさ、かみすぎるとさ、耳がいかれない？
turns.english: But if you blow your nose too much, doesn't it mess up your ears?
turns.note: caption-verified; かむ means blowing one's nose

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: それ、かむの下手やね。
turns.english: Then you're bad at blowing your nose.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 鼻の下、赤くなる。
turns.english: The skin under your nose gets red.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: もうなってる、私、鼻の下。
turns.english: Mine already is—under my nose.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 鼻の下赤くなるのは、しょうがない。
turns.english: You can't really avoid the skin under your nose getting red.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: あと、うち両方の鼻にティッシュ詰めるけど。
turns.english: I stuff tissue into both nostrils, though.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 詰めてる。今。
turns.english: I have it stuffed in right now.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: ねえ、配信中に鼻にティッシュ詰めないの、あんた！
turns.english: Hey! Don't stuff tissue in your nose while you're streaming!

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: それきつくない？ 喋りながら口呼吸してるの、今？
turns.english: Isn't that rough? Are you breathing through your mouth while talking right now?

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: そうだよ。
turns.english: Yeah.
turns.note: caption-verified; corrected speaker from caption color

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: え、つら。
turns.english: That sounds miserable.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: つら。
turns.english: That's rough.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 清楚はやりませんよ、そんなこと。
turns.english: A seiso girl wouldn't do that.
turns.note: caption-verified; seiso means wholesome/refined or prim-and-proper in VTuber slang

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: だって、もうそのまま垂れてくるから。
turns.english: But otherwise it just keeps dripping out.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: あ、びっくりした。「もう清楚は捨てたんですけど」かと思った。

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: ほんとは甘えたい部分を持ってるけど、恋人の前だけバブバブ。
turns.english: You secretly have a side that wants affection, and only go babu-babu in front of your partner.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: バブバブしてんだ～。
turns.english: So you do go all babu-babu.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: そういうことだ。想像に任せますね、そこは。
turns.english: That's what it means. I'll leave that part to your imagination.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: ちゃっかりうさぎちゃんは何なの？
turns.english: What does Chakkari Usagi mean?
turns.note: caption-verified; corrected speaker from caption color

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: ちゃっかりうさぎは、うちも結構一途みたいな感じなんだけど。ただ、その人を一途に愛すってより、「本当に大丈夫か？」みたいなのをちゃんと分析するらしい。
turns.english: Chakkari Usagi is apparently pretty devoted too, but rather than blindly loving one person, it carefully analyzes whether that person is really a good choice.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: 出た。ちゃっかりうさぎ来た。ちゃっかりうさぎだから。
turns.english: There it is—the shrewd-rabbit side came out. That's why I'm a Chakkari Usagi.
turns.note: caption-verified first part; final phrase inferred from ASR

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: ちゃんと考えてるんだ。
turns.english: So you actually think it through.

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: ちなみに、ちゃっかりうさぎと隠れベイビーは、幸せな結婚をしやすい恋愛タイプらしい。
turns.english: Apparently, by the way, Chakkari Usagi and Kakure Baby are romance types likely to have happy marriages.

turns.speaker: HIZUKI_YUI
turns.japanese: え、やった。
turns.english: Yes!

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: え、待って。「最後の恋人」は苦労しそうじゃない？
turns.english: Wait—doesn't “The Last Lover” sound like the type that suffers?

turns.speaker: SHIRAYUKI_REID
turns.japanese: 「最後の恋人」は、たぶん重すぎて苦労する。
turns.english: “The Last Lover” probably suffers because they're too emotionally intense.

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 重くない。
turns.english: I'm not intense.
turns.note: ASR and context; 重い means emotionally heavy or intense here

turns.speaker: AIZAWA_EMA
turns.japanese: 私、でも重いのかな。
turns.english: ...Or maybe I am.
